title: Air Medical Transport

source.boundary: Actual Air Medical Transport title block in right column of page 9 through references in left column of page 13, before actual Mass Gatherings title. Exclude Chapter 2 above starting title and Chapter 4 right column/below ending title.
source.verification: Vocabulary occurrence and boundaries only, not current clinical recommendations or mechanistic entailment.

scope: Sixteen selected terms. Broad learned associations, not exhaustive chapter coverage, source-derived medical narration, generator prompts or claims of novelty.

table_locations.aortic dissection: Table 3-3, critically ill medical or surgical patients

entries.cue: Helicopter with an oversized recognizable rotor.
entries.reason: The familiar aircraft silhouette is enough; a new pun is unnecessary. Rotor emphasis reinforces the category. No aircraft performance or transport-selection claim.

entries.cue: Airplane wings visibly fixed in place by exaggerated bolts.
entries.reason: Ordinary airplane silhouette plus fixed/fastened meaning. Bolts are playful emphasis, not an aircraft construction diagram or implication that helicopter blades are unsecured.

entries.cue: Queasy passenger with a sick bag in a tilted aircraft cabin.
entries.reason: Familiar travel situation needs no exact phonetic bridge. Tilt and context convey motion without demanding every viewer exclude all other nausea causes. Not a diagnosis or treatment cue.

entries.cue: Blood-drop character beside a nearly empty oxygen tank.
entries.reason: Blood identity gives context while scarce oxygen supplies the low-state cue. Tank quantity is a metaphor, not an arterial measurement, cause, saturation value or oxygen-treatment instruction.

entries.cue: Dry shriveled sponge beside an almost empty water bottle.
entries.reason: Dryness and depleted water are familiar rather than arbitrary. Does not diagnose dehydration from appearance or specify fluid treatment. No need for a uniquely medical-looking sponge.

entries.cue: Boy wearing a judge's wig beside a large balloon.
entries.cue_scope: Name cue only: boy/Boyle plus law/judge; balloon supplies gas context
entries.reason: Near-sound name and familiar legal role; not an exact homophone or a complete representation of the physical law. Avoid boiling imagery that could misleadingly suggest a temperature-change law.

entries.cue: Large gas bubble lodged in a transparent branching vessel model.
entries.reason: Simple bubble-in-vessel relation can support learned recall without depicting every qualifier. Does not encode cerebral or arterial modifiers, source of gas, indication or treatment.

entries.cue: Air balloon in the space between a lung model and a transparent chest shell.
entries.cue_scope: Pneumothorax family, not plural count or subtype
entries.reason: Air outside lung within chest is the intended spatial metaphor. Balloon is not a literal foreign body or treatment; do not require plural object counts merely because the source term is plural. Anatomical lesson claims need separate source checking.

entries.cue: Medieval flail resting against a large treasure chest.
entries.reason: Two familiar objects recover the phrase without anatomical detail. Does not encode injury mechanism, rib criteria, physiology or treatment; treasure-chest meaning is an intentional bridge, not confusion.

entries.cue: Transparent chest shell with conspicuous red liquid surrounding a lung model.
entries.reason: Color is anchored by recognizable blood-like liquid and chest context rather than an arbitrary color legend. Not a volume threshold, detailed diagnostic illustration or procedural guide.

entries.cue: Heart character squeezed in a tight transparent fluid-filled pouch.
entries.reason: A useful conceptual relationship without needing every diagnostic sign. Does not say all fluid collections cause tamponade or encode a clinical threshold, etiology or drainage procedure.

entries.cue: Aorta model with its wall visibly peeling into separate layers.
entries.reason: Ordinary structural depiction can be useful; no forced pun required. Use layered separation rather than a vessel cut cleanly in half. No classification, propagation, rupture or treatment claim.

entries.cue: Spinal cord model visibly squeezed by a broad clamp.
entries.reason: Anatomical identity plus a familiar squeeze. Reuses the catalog's generic compression grammar but is a newly recorded chapter composition, not a new primitive. Clamp is metaphorical, not a treatment or assertion of a particular cause.

entries.cue: Limb model downstream of a closed red supply tap and visibly depleted supply tube.
entries.reason: Simple supply metaphor, not a unique name cipher. The closed tap illustrates one recall relationship, not a claim that every ischemic state has a complete arterial blockage. No pulse criteria or therapy encoded.

entries.cue: A statue with a conspicuous cartoon shaking pose.
entries.cue_scope: Provisional status/statue name bridge plus broad seizure association
entries.reason: Potentially teachable, but this particular statue/shaking proposal needs a clearer learned bridge before retention. Not rejected merely for lacking a duration threshold. Do not equate all seizures, tremor or all status presentations with visible shaking.

Cricket supplies only a weak opening fragment; the neck prop adds little to recover the remainder. Keep as an ingredient idea, not a useful complete bridge yet. No improvised cutting or procedure depiction.
